_what: R1 STOP-LOSS, as numbers a program can read. Consumed by pipeline/scripts/rule_gate.cap_check via load_caps().
_why_this_file_exists: R1 is the first rule the owner adopted and it has never once been enforced. `cap_check` is a working function with four passing tests that `check()` did not call, for a reason no amount of code could fix: it takes a ledger row carrying `cap_rounds` / `cap_full_frames`, and NO UNIT HAS EVER DECLARED THEM. The curriculum ledger (qa/reproduction-curriculum.md) has a `rounds | full frames` column, but those are ACTUALS, it is a markdown table nothing parses, and it has no TRN-002 row at all. So the numbers lived nowhere a machine could reach and the rule stayed a document for 34 rounds. This file is the smallest thing that changes that.
_law: R3 — only the owner sets or extends a cap, once per unit, with the new number AND its reason written here BEFORE the next render. A cap raised after the breach, without a reason, is not a cap.
_counting: Both counts are derived from disk by rule_gate.count_rounds / count_full_frames, never typed. ROUNDS = canonical spec_r<N>.json files in the lane (bracket variants like spec_r30w110.json do not count — they are one round's experiments, not rounds). FULL FRAMES = PNGs in the lane's render dir at the spec's own image size. THE SECOND ONE IS COUNTED BY PIXELS, NOT BY FILENAME, and the difference is not pedantic: 137 of this lane's PNGs lack the `_quick` token and only 44 are actually full frames — the rest are crops, comparison sheets and target excerpts. A cap counted by filename would have been wrong by 3x on its first run.

DELIV-001.reason: ORD-2026-07-28's builder half, carried out at p2r49: `rule_gate.count_rounds_room` counts the highest ROUND with a gate artefact (a round that closed and spent), and `count_full_frames_room` counts beauty PNGs at the deliverable size with the id/mat masks removed — the pixel test alone over-counted this lane by very nearly 2x, because both masks are written at exactly DELIVERABLE_RES. The spend now prints at every gate run and at session open. Setting the number is his half: the caps file's own _law says only the owner sets or extends a cap, and blocking the lane on that would halt it on an unanswered ask, which R3 forbids by name.
DELIV-001.quick_frames_uncapped: Same as TRN-002 and for the same reason: R5 wants the playblast rung cheap and frequent, and capping it would punish the thing that prevents full frames.

TRN-002.declared_by: owner order (`ลุยหมด`), on the builder's recommendation of 42/55
TRN-002.reason: A FINISHING budget, not a fresh one, and it is already 170% of the rounds and 119% of the full frames that closed TRN-001 (20 / 37). What is left is countable: r34 is built and unrendered (1), the light has to be re-derived because the geometry moved under it (1-2), etagere_objects needs a measurement pass and a build (1-2), and garments needs a glTF ingest path before it needs anything else (1-2). That is 4-8 rounds and 42/55 sits at the top of it. IF IT RUNS OUT AND THE UNIT IS NOT CLOSED, THE PROBLEM IS NOT THE BUDGET. The alternative the owner declined was 34/44 — the current spend, which would fire R1 on the very next render and force the close-or-continue decision immediately; that reading of R1 is the stricter one and it remains available at the cost of one number.
TRN-002.quick_frames_uncapped: Deliberate. R5 wants the playblast rung cheap and frequent, and this lane's ratio is 114 quick to 44 full (2.6:1), which is the behaviour the rule asks for. Capping quick renders would punish the thing that prevents full ones.
